questions.q: Which statements take an exclusive (X) lock on the rows they affect?
options: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE
SELECT only
Only DELETE, never INSERT or UPDATE
None — writes use shared locks too
questions.explain: Any statement that modifies data takes an exclusive lock on the rows it changes.

questions.q: How many transactions can hold an exclusive lock on the same resource at once?
options: Only one
Any number, like shared locks
Exactly two
Unlimited, but only during the same session
questions.explain: Exclusive locks are incompatible with every other lock, including another exclusive lock, so only one transaction can hold one at a time.

questions.q: While Session A holds an exclusive lock on a row, what happens to Session B's plain SELECT against that same row?
options: It blocks, because a shared-lock request conflicts with an existing exclusive lock
It succeeds immediately, returning the old committed value
It succeeds immediately, returning Session A's uncommitted value
It throws a syntax error
questions.explain: Exclusive locks conflict with shared locks too, so a reader blocks behind a writer's open transaction.

questions.q: How long is an exclusive lock held, compared to a shared lock under READ COMMITTED?
options: Until COMMIT or ROLLBACK, for the rest of the transaction — a shared lock is released as soon as that individual read finishes
Exactly the same duration as a shared lock
Only until the next statement runs, then it's automatically released
Exclusive locks are never released until the server restarts
questions.explain: Unlike a shared lock's early release, an exclusive lock is held for the remaining life of the transaction.

questions.q: What would happen if SQL Server allowed two transactions to hold exclusive locks on the same row at the same time?
options: Whichever write finished last would silently overwrite the other, with no error or warning
SQL Server would merge both writes automatically into one correct value
Nothing — exclusive locks don't actually prevent any real problem
Both writes would be queued and applied in alphabetical order
questions.explain: Exclusive locks exist specifically to prevent two writers from corrupting the same row by writing to it simultaneously.
